label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's a reply you can post:

---

Hello everyone, it's Hélène from Pétrin Doré. My nephew showed me this thread and I think I have to answer now, even if I wanted to keep this for the reopening. Thank you D. Bergeron for asking the question in a polite way. You deserve a straight answer, so here it is.

**We are not closing. We bought the building.**

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right: the building was sold in the fall. It was sold to me! M. Ferland, who owns the building, is 81 and retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell to me before anybody else, and we signed at the notary on December 15. So no condos, no bank, no vape shop. Just the bakery, and a bakery that will stay here.

M. Ferland has come every morning for 17 years to buy his baguette pas trop cuite. I will tell you, he cried a little at the notary, and I did too, a little. It's a good ending for both of us.

**So what is the closing for?**

We close from January 4 to 18 for renovations. Here is what is happening:

- A new deck oven with 4 decks, coming from a supplier in Laval. The old oven is from 1998 and it broke down 3 times this year. I am tired of praying every night before the 4 a.m. start, and I think the bread will be better too.
- We are taking the space at the back, the old storage of the dépanneur. There will be 6 small tables, so finally people can sit down with their coffee and their pain de campagne. I know, it's small, but it's a start.

We reopen **Tuesday, January 19, at 7h**.

**About the carnets**

I want to be very clear about this, because I understand why people worry. We sold 214 carnets in October, $60 for 12 loaves. Every one of them is still good. There is no expiry date. Nothing changes, you use them like before, whenever you want. And to say thank you for your trust, every carnet holder gets one free croissant in January when we reopen, just show me the carnet.

noodle_and_crumb, your 7 loaves are safe, and I'm happy you have a carnet.

And if somebody is really not comfortable, and wants the money back for the carnet, just come and see me and I give it back. No question, no problem, no bad feeling. I mean it.

I will be honest, the word "scam" hurt me a bit. I have been on this street for 17 years, since March 2009. But I also understand. Mile End has lost so many small shops, and people are right to be careful when they see a sign and shelves that are empty. I would probably wonder too.

**About the sign and the shelves**

The sign is my fault, or my nephew's fault, a little. Thomas wrote it at 6 in the morning, and "grande nouvelle" was his idea. I said ok without thinking, and I did not imagine how it would sound from the street. Sorry for the worry, that was not the goal.

The shelves that looked half empty on the 28th: we sold everything for Christmas Eve. 400 bûches, and a lot of bread with them. It has nothing to do with closing. It was just a very good week.

**To the people living upstairs**

For the 3 apartments above the bakery: you are staying. Same tenants, same rent. I promised each of you in writing, and I will keep it. Please don't worry about the works, and if the noise or the dust is too much for you in those two weeks, come and talk to me and we find a solution.

**Thank you**

Priya, thank you for what you wrote. And thank you to everyone who defended us in this thread without even knowing the whole story. It really touched me. I read that and I thought, ok, we are in the right neighbourhood. Also thank you to all the customers who came in the last 17 years, I don't say it enough.

**Come celebrate with us**

I invite everybody to the reopening on **Saturday, January 23**. There will be coffee, and a piece of the new bread for free, baked in the new oven. You don't need a carnet, you don't need to buy anything, just come, say hello, and sit at one of the new little tables if you can find a place!

I'm sorry again that you had to read rumours before you could read the truth. It was my choice to keep the surprise, and next time I will think about it more. But I am very happy now to say it out loud: we are staying, and we are only getting started.

See you on the 19th, at 7h, and on the 23rd for the party.

Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré, 5 rue Fairmount

---

That comes to about 800 words. A couple of things to check before you post: the free croissant is written as "in January when we reopen" (so from the 19th on), and the refund offer says people come to see you at the bakery, so if you'd rather they wait until after the 19th, add a line about that.
